verdicts.tldr: once a heading holds an icon, every heading id in the document is regenerated from a fresh newLinearIDs(), so explicit {#id} attributes and a caller's own ID generator are overwritten
verdicts.details: The transformer's comment says 'Only auto IDs', but line 190 only checks that an id attribute exists, so an id set by parser.WithAttribute from `## Intro {#custom}` is replaced with the generated one. Line 182 builds its own newLinearIDs() instead of pc.IDs(), so a caller passing parser.WithIDs gets a different generator for every heading. In-tree the realm renderer has WithAutoHeadingID and no WithAttribute (render_config.go:36), NewGnoParserContext installs the same newLinearIDs (context.go:25), and documentationGM uses WithAttribute without the Gno extension (render.go:101-107), so nothing ships it today. Fix: generate from pc.IDs() and skip headings whose id did not come from auto-generation, or say in the ExtIcons doc that it requires auto ids and no attribute ids.
verdicts.evidence: Read: ext_icons.go:182 `ids := newLinearIDs()`; :190 `if _, ok := h.AttributeString("id"); ok && h.Lines().Len() > 0 {` then :192 SetAttributeString. grep 'WithAttribute()' gno.land contribs: only render.go:107 (docOpts, extensions are Highlighting, ExtCodeExpand, ExtEmphasis). render_config.go:36 WithAutoHeadingID only. context.go:25 parser.WithIDs(newLinearIDs()). No goldmark run.
verdicts.verify_by: grep -rn 'WithAttribute()' gno.land contribs --include='*.go'; build goldmark.New(WithParserOptions(parser.WithAutoHeadingID(), parser.WithAttribute()), WithExtensions(NewGnoExtension())) and render the two headings

verdicts.tldr: FuzzIconRender reports an event handler for any labeled icon whose label holds a word starting with 'on', so fuzzing stops on a safe render
verdicts.details: The oracle cuts each <svg tag at its first '>' and looks for ' on' in it. That span ends with the aria-label value, which renderIcon writes from the user's label, so `label="turn on"` gives `aria-label="turn on"` and the check fires. The fuzzer reports a crash for safe output, and a real failure is harder to find among these. Fix: match an attribute name, e.g. regexp `\son[a-z]+\s*=` over the tag with the aria-label value removed.
verdicts.evidence: Read: ext_icons_test.go:170 `if tag, _, _ := strings.Cut(svg, ">"); strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(tag), " on") {`; ext_icons.go:255-257 write ` role="img" aria-label="` + label + `">`, so the label sits inside the cut span. Fuzz corpus not run.
verdicts.verify_by: add testdata/fuzz/FuzzIconRender/b3 with `go test fuzz v1\nstring("<gno-icon name=\"star\" label=\"turn on\" />")` and run go test -run FuzzIconRender: expect the fatal

verdicts.tldr: `<gno-icon name=star/>` renders the hint 'write it self-closing' although the author wrote `/>`
verdicts.details: scanGnoTag reads an unquoted value up to whitespace or '>', so `name=star/>` gives the value `star/`, the tag ends on a plain '>', and SelfClosing is false. renderIcon then emits the self-closing hint, which tells the author to do what they already did. The golden pins this output on purpose, and scanGnoTag is shared with #6298 and #6299, where `href=/r/x/` needs the slash kept. Fix: in the !SelfClosing branch, when n.Name ends in '/', say to quote the name or put a space before `/>`.

Unquoted value eats the slash:

`.
verdicts.verify_by: render `<gno-icon name=star/> x` through newProductionLikeMarkdown and read the comment

verdicts.tldr: the ADR sizes the 1,000-icon cap at 2.3 KB per icon, but an escaped label can more than double that: about 5.2 KB per icon, about 5.2 MB at the cap
verdicts.details: renderIcon writes the label through gmhtml.DefaultWriter.Write, which escapes `"` to the 6-byte `"`. The 512-byte tag bound leaves room for about 481 quotes in `<gno-icon name=pure label='"""…' />`. That is about 2.9 KB of aria-label on top of pure's roughly 2.3 KB glyph (its icons_gen.go entry is a 2,269-byte line). The cap still holds, well under the pre-cap 105 MB page, but the ADR's sizing and its 3.5 MB figure leave out the label. The 5.2 KB is arithmetic from the read, not a measurement. Fix: state the bound as glyph plus up to about 6x the label bytes, or cap the label length.
verdicts.evidence: Read: ext_icons.go:255-257 `gmhtml.DefaultWriter.Write(w, n.Label)`; maxIconTagLen = 512 (:91) also caps the label; awk length of the `"pure":` line in icons_gen.go: 2269. ADR:83 'Each icon writes up to 2.3 KB'. Not converted.
verdicts.verify_by: One-off Go test in package markdown: Convert strings.Repeat("<gno-icon name=pure label='" + strings.Repeat(`"`, 481) + "' />\n\n", 1000) through newProductionLikeMarkdown with NewGnoParserContext; expect len(out)/1000 <= 2.3 KB per the ADR, observe about 5.2 KB.

verdicts.tldr: `make icons` fetches the upstream archive with no timeout, so a stalled connection hangs instead of failing
verdicts.details: fetchUpstream calls http.Get, which uses http.DefaultClient with Timeout 0, and the file sets no deadline anywhere. A half-open or stalled connection to codeload leaves the maintainer's `make icons` blocked with no error until they interrupt it. This only affects the developer tool. Fix: use an &http.Client{Timeout: time.Minute} for the download.
verdicts.evidence: Read: main.go:122 `resp, err := http.Get(upstreamArchive + upstreamCommit)`; grep 'Timeout\|http\.' main.go: lines 122 and 127 only, no Timeout. Hang not reproduced.
verdicts.verify_by: Read main.go:122: http.Get(upstreamArchive + upstreamCommit) uses http.DefaultClient (Timeout 0). Check: point upstreamArchive at a listener that accepts and never answers (nc -l), run go -C gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/tools run ./cmd/iconset gno.land/pkg/gnoweb: never returns.

verdicts.tldr: a label that decodes to blank, like ` ` or ` `, renders role="img" with a blank aria-label and suppresses the alone-in-link hint
verdicts.details: parseIconTag trims the raw label bytes, so ` ` stays non-empty. renderIcon then takes the labeled branch and DefaultWriter.Write resolves the reference to a space. The hint at line 266 is gated on len(n.Label) == 0, so `[<gno-icon name="star" label=" " />](/r/docs)` gives a link with no accessible name, and the author is not told. No test or golden covers an entity-only label. Fix: decide blankness on the decoded label (util.ResolveEntityNames/ResolveNumericReferences, then util.IsBlank) and treat a blank one as absent.
